title: Payment Ledger

functional: Record payments, refunds, and transfers as double-entry journal entries.
Expose account balances and an immutable transaction history.
Accept retried requests without moving money twice.
Settle with external payment providers and banks.
Reconcile provider statements and handle unmatched entries.
nonFunctional: Committed ledger reads and writes target 99.99% monthly availability.
Every transaction must balance: total debits equal total credits.
Writes for one account should be strongly consistent.
The ledger must remain auditable for seven years.
External provider outages must not block internal bookkeeping.

checklist: Transfer and refund API with idempotency
Double-entry data model and balance invariant
followUps: How would you support multiple currencies and exchange rates?
How would you prove that no money was created or destroyed over a period?
How would you handle a provider that settles a payment twice?
What changes if the ledger must span multiple regions with local writes?
commonMistakes: Storing a mutable balance as the source of truth instead of postings.
Using a client-generated request id without a server-side idempotency record.
Updating or deleting journal entries to fix a mistake.
Calling the payment provider inside the database transaction.
Assuming at-least-once delivery is the same as exactly-once execution.
attribution: Original scenario by the Base Case contributors.
